Use Tier 2: change the training input construction so the final-query objective receives intact history, matching inference. Focus on data_processing_and_feature_engineering and training_evaluation. The current sampler masks approximately 20% of historical items while also predicting the final item, whereas inference masks only the final query. This creates a concrete training–inference mismatch; whether it limits validation performance remains a hypothesis, and the unsuccessful relative-bias, convolution, and larger-negative trials have not tested it.

For each sampled training prefix, construct two views with the same target and context window: a prediction-aligned view containing intact preceding history and one final query mask, and the existing corrupted view for auxiliary historical reconstruction. Run both views through the same MaskedSASRec with shared parameters, computing final-target loss exclusively from the intact-history view and auxiliary loss exclusively from masked historical positions in the corrupted view. Retain the existing equal weighting when auxiliary targets exist, use final loss alone otherwise, and preserve the 256-negative sampled-softmax formulation and target-collision masking. Never expose the final target in either input view; this is one jointly trained network per category, with one forward pass per prediction.

Keep the backbone, optimizer, prefix sampling, supplied splits, seeds, validation candidates, checkpoint selection, and stopping rules unchanged to isolate this representation change. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, trial-local artifacts, and the predictor writer’s reconstruction of exactly one selected checkpoint per category; verify that the intact training view matches prediction_sequence for the same context. Compare authoritative host macro validation HR@10 against 0.580 and report category scores and actual GPU cost, accounting for the additional training forward pass within the existing time limits; leave held-out evaluation to the host.
